subject: Retaining all the levels of a factor in a legend (even unused ones)

messages.author: 410e477af3aeaf0d
messages.subject: Retaining all the levels of a factor in a legend (even unused ones)
parts:
Hi,

Does anyone know how I can retain all the levels of a factor in the legend even if they don't appear on the plot? I'm creating two plots of subsets of the same dataset. It just happens that the factor I'm using to colour the plot shapes is bisected into two groups by the subsetting. I want to be able to create a single legend spanning both plots which contains all the values (not just those in one subset). The problem currently is that plots reuse the same colours for different levels (and unused factor levels disappear).

I've tried to use the mtcars data set to make a little example showing what I mean:

data(mtcars)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)

# Turn some of data into factors
mtcars$gear <- factor(mtcars$gear)
mtcars$carb <- factor(mtcars$carb)

# Create two subsets of data with divergent properties
data.a <- mtcars[mtcars$gear %in% c("4","5") & mtcars$carb %in% c("1","2"), ]
data.b <- mtcars[mtcars$gear %in% c("1","2","3") & !mtcars$carb %in% c("1","2"), ]

# All the levels still appear in the subsets (e.g. I've not used droplevels())
levels(data.a$carb)
levels(data.b$carb)

plot.a <- ggplot(data.a, aes(cyl, mpg)) + geom_point(aes(colour = carb)) + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position="top")
plot.b <- ggplot(data.b, aes(cyl, mpg)) + geom_point(aes(colour = carb)) + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position="top")
grid.arrange(plot.a, plot.b, ncol=2)

What you should see are two side-by-side plots with the legends at the top. Both will contain a pink and blue key entry, however, these colours will not refer to the same carb values. 

Thanks,
Alastair

messages.subject: Re: Retaining all the levels of a factor in a legend (even unused ones)
parts:
Brian Diggs pointed this out yesterday to help fix a legend for an animation.

plot.b<-plot.b+scale_colour_discrete(drop=FALSE)
plot.a<-plot.a+scale_colour_discrete(drop=FALSE)
grid.arrange(plot.a, plot.b, ncol=2)
